thesis: Oklo builds compact 15-75 MW factory-built Aurora Powerhouse fast reactors on a 'build, own, operate' model with long-term PPAs, targeting AI data centers and industrial off-takers. Q2 2026 marked the company's first reported revenue ($1.2M), while the Groves Isotope Test Reactor achieved first criticality following DOE startup authorization, a major de-risking milestone. A Trump-administration-backed ~$200M advanced-nuclear-for-AI initiative alongside Microsoft, Nvidia and X-energy validates demand, and the Meta 1.2 GW Ohio campus remains an anchor contract. With ~$3.0B in total liquidity ($1.6B cash and equivalents + $1.4B marketable securities) after raising $1.9B via ATM equity in 2026, Oklo is funded through late-2027/2028 first commercial operation, but NRC licensing risk (Aurora-INL), HALEU fuel supply scarcity, and extreme volatility/beta remain the key risks.

financials.cash: $3.0B total liquidity ($1.6B cash and equivalents + $1.4B marketable securities)

drivers: Groves Isotope Test Reactor first criticality already achieved, validating the fuel and licensing pathway
Aurora-INL progresses through NRC licensing without major delays
Meta Ohio 1.2 GW campus proceeds and additional LOIs convert to binding PPAs
Trump-administration ~$200M advanced-nuclear-for-AI initiative accelerates deployment and policy tailwinds
First commercial operation confirmed for late 2027/2028, re-rating the stock toward its prior highs

risks: NRC licensing delays push first commercial operation into 2029-2030
HALEU fuel supply constraints limit deployment speed
First-of-a-kind commissioning issues emerge at Groves or Aurora-INL
Continued nuclear-sector profit-taking and high beta drive further downside
LOI pipeline fails to convert to binding, financeable PPAs

base_case.assumptions: Groves first criticality achieved and Aurora-INL advances through NRC licensing with modest slippage; Meta Ohio Phase 1 and initial PPA conversions proceed; ~$3.0B liquidity funds the plan without near-term dilution; stock trades on execution milestones between its 52-week low and prior highs. Consensus avg target ~$79.88 implies roughly 70% upside from current levels.

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings reported — first revenue ($1.2M vs ~$72K est), adjusted loss $0.28/share, ~$3.0B liquidity
Groves Isotope Test Reactor achieved first criticality following DOE startup authorization — major de-risking milestone completed
Aurora-INL progress and NRC licensing advancement
LOI-to-PPA conversions and Meta 1.2 GW Ohio campus timeline
First commercial operation — major derisking event

key_risks: NRC licensing risk — no non-water-cooled commercial reactor has yet been licensed; delays push out first revenue
HALEU fuel supply scarcity constrains deployment (Russia banned as supplier)
First-of-a-kind technology execution risk at Groves and Aurora-INL commercial scale
Extreme valuation and sentiment volatility — stock round-tripped from ~$194 to ~$47 with a beta of 1.20; drawdowns can be sharp and sentiment-led
Pre-revenue duration until late 2027/2028; first commercial operation is ~2 years out, testing investor patience
